392	+++ b/lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart
393	@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
394	+// The constructor keeps a public named param (`recorder`) distinct from
395	+// the private field it initializes, matching
396	+// `vault_repository_impl.dart`'s documented convention.
397	+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
398	+import 'dart:io';
399	+
400	+import 'package:path_provider/path_provider.dart';
401	+// Aliased — `record`'s own `AudioRecorder` would otherwise clash with
402	+// nothing in this file today, but the alias keeps every reference to the
403	+// package explicit, per Code Map.
404	+import 'package:record/record.dart' as record_pkg;
405	+
406	+import '../../domain/services/mic_recorder.dart';
407	+
408	+/// Wraps `package:record`'s `AudioRecorder` behind the [MicRecorder] port.
409	+/// A `get_it` singleton (Code Map/`capture_injection.dart`) — one real
410	+/// recorder for the app's lifetime, reused across every Insertion Modal
411	+/// open, never recreated per "+" tap the way `AudioEntryCubit` itself is.
412	+class RecordMicRecorder implements MicRecorder {
413	+  RecordMicRecorder({required record_pkg.AudioRecorder recorder})
414	+    : _recorder = recorder;
415	+
416	+  final record_pkg.AudioRecorder _recorder;
417	+
418	+  /// Set by [start], cleared by [stop]/[cancel] — [stop] has no other way
419	+  /// to learn how long the session ran, since `AudioRecorder.stop()` only
420	+  /// ever returns the output path.
421	+  DateTime? _startedAt;
422	+
423	+  /// Set by [start], cleared by [stop]/[cancel] — tracked independently
424	+  /// of `_recorder`'s own "delete on cancel" contract (Review finding:
425	+  /// that contract was asserted in this class's own doc comment but
426	+  /// never independently verified) so [cancel] can delete the file
427	+  /// itself rather than relying solely on the plugin's behavior.
428	+  String? _currentPath;
429	+
430	+  @override
431	+  Future<bool> hasPermission() => _recorder.hasPermission();
432	+
433	+  @override
434	+  Future<void> start() async {
435	+    final dir = await getTemporaryDirectory();
436	+    final path =
437	+        '${dir.path}/cerne_audio_entry_'
438	+        '${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.wav';
439	+    await _recorder.start(
440	+      // 16kHz mono matches `whisper_ggml`'s own expected input exactly
441	+      // (its internal ffmpeg conversion step — `WhisperAudioConvert` —
442	+      // falls back to passing the file through unconverted when ffmpeg
443	+      // is unavailable, which only works if it's already in this shape).
444	+      const record_pkg.RecordConfig(
445	+        encoder: record_pkg.AudioEncoder.wav,
446	+        sampleRate: 16000,
447	+        numChannels: 1,
448	+      ),
449	+      path: path,
450	+    );
451	+    _startedAt = DateTime.now();
452	+    _currentPath = path;
453	+  }
454	+
455	+  @override
456	+  Future<MicRecording?> stop() async {
457	+    final path = await _recorder.stop();
458	+    final startedAt = _startedAt;
459	+    _startedAt = null;
460	+    _currentPath = null;
461	+    if (path == null || startedAt == null) {
462	+      return null;
463	+    }
464	+    return MicRecording(
465	+      path: path,
466	+      durationSeconds: DateTime.now().difference(startedAt).inSeconds,
467	+    );
468	+  }
469	+
470	+  @override
471	+  Future<void> cancel() async {
472	+    _startedAt = null;
473	+    final path = _currentPath;
474	+    _currentPath = null;
475	+    await _recorder.cancel();
476	+    // Review finding: don't rely solely on the plugin's own "cancel
477	+    // deletes the file" contract — delete it ourselves too, best-effort,
478	+    // so this class's own doc comment stays true regardless of the
479	+    // underlying plugin's actual behavior.
480	+    if (path != null) {
481	+      try {
482	+        await File(path).delete();
483	+      } catch (_) {
484	+        // Best-effort — the plugin may have already deleted it itself,
485	+        // or it may never have existed (e.g. a very early cancel).
486	+      }
487	+    }
488	+  }
489	+
490	+  @override
491	+  Stream<double> get amplitudeStream => _recorder
492	+      .onAmplitudeChanged(const Duration(milliseconds: 200))
493	+      .map(_normalize);
494	+
495	+  /// `record`'s own `Amplitude.current` is dBFS, roughly -45 (near
496	+  /// silence, in practice — the package's own floor is -160 but normal
497	+  /// mic noise never gets that quiet) to 0 (loudest) — rescaled to a
498	+  /// 0.0–1.0 range the waveform widget can use directly, with no
499	+  /// `package:record` type ever crossing the [MicRecorder] boundary.
500	+  double _normalize(record_pkg.Amplitude amplitude) {
501	+    const floorDb = -45.0;
502	+    final clamped = amplitude.current.clamp(floorDb, 0.0);
503	+    return (clamped - floorDb) / -floorDb;
504	+  }
505	+}

579	+/// A finished microphone recording — the on-disk file [path] plus its

581	+/// Dart, not `package:record`'s own types — keeps this port, and every
582	+/// caller that depends on it (`AudioEntryCubit`), decoupled from that
583	+/// package's shape (Boundaries: "decouple the cubit from both packages").
584	+class MicRecording {
585	+  const MicRecording({required this.path, required this.durationSeconds});
586	+
587	+  final String path;
588	+  final int durationSeconds;
589	+}

591	+/// Capture's own mic-recording port — the `record`-backed
592	+/// `RecordMicRecorder` is the only implementation (Code Map), mirroring
593	+/// `EntriesRepository`'s port convention (an abstract class in `domain/`,
594	+/// a concrete `data/` class wrapping the real package, injected via
595	+/// `capture_injection.dart`). `AudioEntryCubit` depends on this interface
596	+/// only, never on `package:record` directly (RNF06-style boundary,
597	+/// extended here to any native package, not just `data/`).
598	+abstract class MicRecorder {

600	+  /// default, requests if not yet granted) microphone permission — the
601	+  /// one permission check this story ever performs (Boundaries: "no

604	+
605	+  /// Starts a new recording session to a fresh temp file. Callers must

609	+
610	+  /// Stops the current recording session, returning its file path and

613	+

618	+  Future<void> cancel();

624	+}

640	+
641	+/// `AudioEntryCubit`'s own sealed state hierarchy — separate from
642	+/// `TextEntryState` (Boundaries: "own sealed `AudioCaptureState`,
643	+/// separate from `TextEntryState`"). Unlike `TextEntryState`, no common
644	+/// base-class field: the 5 variants don't share a uniform shape the way
645	+/// every `TextEntryState` always carries `activeTab`/`text` — [AudioIdle]
646	+/// genuinely has nothing in common with [AudioTranscribed], for instance.
647	+sealed class AudioCaptureState {
648	+  const AudioCaptureState();
649	+}
650	+
651	+/// The state immediately after the modal opens on the Áudio tab exits
652	+/// (Never: this story's trivial cross-tab case), and the state a fresh
653	+/// `AudioEntryCubit` always starts in.
654	+class AudioIdle extends AudioCaptureState {
655	+  const AudioIdle();
656	+}
657	+
658	+/// Recording in progress — [elapsedSeconds] backs the running monospace
659	+/// timer (Acceptance Criteria) and ticks once per second via
660	+/// `AudioEntryCubit`'s own internal `Timer.periodic`.
661	+class AudioRecording extends AudioCaptureState {
662	+  const AudioRecording({required this.elapsedSeconds});
663	+
664	+  final int elapsedSeconds;
665	+}
666	+
667	+/// Recording stopped, `AudioTranscriber.transcribe()` in flight —
668	+/// `InsertionModal`'s own `_AudioTab` freezes the waveform at 35% opacity
669	+/// for the whole duration of this state (Acceptance Criteria).
670	+class AudioProcessing extends AudioCaptureState {
671	+  const AudioProcessing({required this.path, required this.durationSeconds});
672	+
673	+  final String path;
674	+  final int durationSeconds;
675	+}
676	+
677	+/// Transcription succeeded (even to an empty string) — [text] is editable
678	+/// before Salvar (Acceptance Criteria), mirrored into this state by
679	+/// `AudioEntryCubit.updateText` the same way `TextEntryCubit.updateText`
680	+/// mirrors the Texto field. [saving] is this story's `TextEntrySaving`
681	+/// equivalent folded into one state instead of a separate sibling class —
682	+/// both [path]/[durationSeconds] (needed for the eventual `create()` call)
683	+/// stay fixed across a save attempt, so there's nothing a sibling state
684	+/// would add that a boolean field doesn't already cover just as clearly.
685	+class AudioTranscribed extends AudioCaptureState {
686	+  const AudioTranscribed({
687	+    required this.path,
688	+    required this.durationSeconds,
689	+    required this.text,
690	+    required this.saving,
691	+  });
692	+
693	+  final String path;
694	+  final int durationSeconds;
695	+  final String text;
696	+  final bool saving;
697	+
698	+  AudioTranscribed copyWith({String? text, bool? saving}) => AudioTranscribed(
699	+    path: path,
700	+    durationSeconds: durationSeconds,
701	+    text: text ?? this.text,
702	+    saving: saving ?? this.saving,
703	+  );
704	+}
705	+
706	+/// A save attempt from [AudioTranscribed] succeeded — `InsertionModal`'s
707	+/// listener reacts to this exactly like `TextEntrySaved` (announce, then
708	+/// pop). Terminal, same rationale as `TextEntrySaved`'s own doc.
709	+class AudioSaved extends AudioCaptureState {
710	+  const AudioSaved();
711	+}
712	+
713	+/// The last attempt failed — covers all 3 failure rows of the I/O matrix:
714	+/// - Mic permission denied -> [path]/[durationSeconds] both `null` ("No
715	+///   file to preserve"); [AudioEntryCubit.retry] re-requests permission.
716	+/// - Transcription failed -> [path]/[durationSeconds] carry the preserved
717	+///   file; [AudioEntryCubit.retry] re-transcribes it, never re-records.
718	+/// - Save failed (incl. offline) -> same preserved [path]/
719	+///   [durationSeconds]/[text] semantics as `TextEntryError`; the modal's
720	+///   `_AudioTab` keeps showing the editable text with Salvar re-enabled
721	+///   rather than routing back through [AudioEntryCubit.retry].
722	+class AudioError extends AudioCaptureState {
723	+  const AudioError({
724	+    required this.path,
725	+    required this.durationSeconds,
726	+    required this.message,
727	+    this.text,
728	+  });
729	+
730	+  final String? path;
731	+  final int? durationSeconds;
732	+  final String message;
733	+
734	+  /// Non-null only for a save failure — lets `_AudioTab` keep rendering
735	+  /// the editable text field under the inline error, same as
736	+  /// `TextEntryError`'s own `_TextoTab` rendering.
737	+  final String? text;
738	+}
739	+
740	+/// Drives the Áudio tab's recording -> processing -> transcribed/error
741	+/// pipeline (Intent). A fresh, `get_it`-factory-scoped instance per "+"
742	+/// tap, same convention as `TextEntryCubit` — [MicRecorder]/
743	+/// [AudioTranscriber] themselves stay long-lived `get_it` singletons
744	+/// (`capture_injection.dart`), shared across every modal open the way
745	+/// `EntriesRepository` already is for `TextEntryCubit`.
746	+class AudioEntryCubit extends Cubit<AudioCaptureState> {
747	+  AudioEntryCubit(this._micRecorder, this._audioTranscriber, this._repository)
748	+    : super(const AudioIdle());
749	+
750	+  final MicRecorder _micRecorder;
751	+  final AudioTranscriber _audioTranscriber;
752	+  final EntriesRepository _repository;
753	+
754	+  Timer? _elapsedTimer;
755	+
756	+  /// Bumped by [cancel] so an in-flight [startRecording]/[stopRecording]
757	+  /// continuation can tell "the user already left the Áudio tab while I
758	+  /// was awaiting" apart from "nothing has changed since I started" —
759	+  /// the same role `isClosed` already plays for `close()`, but for a tab
760	+  /// switch that doesn't close the cubit itself (Review finding: without
761	+  /// this, `cancel()` running mid-await either left the recorder running
762	+  /// unobserved, or let a stale `stop()`/transcription result resurrect a
763	+  /// flow the user already left).
764	+  int _generation = 0;
765	+
766	+  /// Forwarded straight from [MicRecorder.amplitudeStream] — lets
767	+  /// `_AudioTab`'s waveform animate without ever importing `package:record`
768	+  /// itself (Boundaries).
769	+  Stream<double> get amplitudeStream => _micRecorder.amplitudeStream;
770	+
771	+  /// Starts recording — called from `InsertionModal`'s tab-switch
772	+  /// listener the instant the Áudio tab becomes active (Acceptance
773	+  /// Criteria: "recording starts immediately"), and again by [retry] when
774	+  /// the last attempt failed before any file ever existed (permission
775	+  /// denied). Ignored while a recording is already in progress, and —
776	+  /// Review finding — ignored once the pipeline has moved past recording
777	+  /// ([AudioProcessing]/[AudioTranscribed]/an [AudioError] that still
778	+  /// carries a file): without this, re-entering the Áudio tab after a
779	+  /// completed transcription silently discarded the transcribed text and
780	+  /// started a brand-new recording over it. Only [AudioIdle] (fresh) or
781	+  /// an [AudioError] with no file (nothing to discard) actually start.
782	+  Future<void> startRecording() async {
783	+    final current = state;
784	+    final canStart =
785	+        current is AudioIdle ||
786	+        (current is AudioError && current.path == null);
787	+    if (!canStart) {
788	+      return;
789	+    }
790	+    final generation = ++_generation;
791	+    final hasPermission = await _micRecorder.hasPermission();
792	+    if (isClosed || generation != _generation) {
793	+      return;
794	+    }
795	+    if (!hasPermission) {
796	+      emit(
797	+        const AudioError(
798	+          path: null,
799	+          durationSeconds: null,
800	+          message:
801	+              'Permissão de microfone negada. Toque em "Tentar novamente" '
802	+              'para permitir o acesso.',
803	+        ),
804	+      );
805	+      return;
806	+    }
807	+    await _micRecorder.start();
808	+    if (isClosed || generation != _generation) {
809	+      // Review finding: `cancel()` bumped `_generation` (the user already
810	+      // left the Áudio tab) while `start()` was in flight — stop/discard
811	+      // the session we just started instead of leaving a live, unobserved
812	+      // recording running.
813	+      unawaited(_micRecorder.cancel());
814	+      return;
815	+    }
816	+    _startElapsedTimer();
817	+    emit(const AudioRecording(elapsedSeconds: 0));
818	+  }
819	+

+---
+title: 'Story 3.2: Audio Entry Capture & On-Device Transcription'
+type: 'feature'

+status: 'done'

+

+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** The Áudio tab is still an idle placeholder (`_IdleTabPlaceholder`) — recording, on-device transcription, and saving a `source=audio` Entry don't exist, and the app has no audio-recording package or microphone-permission handling at all.
+
+**Approach:** Add a new `AudioEntryCubit` (its own sealed state, separate from `TextEntryCubit`) driving the 4-state pipeline — recording → processing → transcribed → error — backed by two new `capture/domain` ports: `MicRecorder` (`record` package) and `AudioTranscriber` (`whisper_ggml`). Extend `Entry`/`EntriesRepository.create` with the optional `mediaDurationSeconds` field the backend contract already reserves. Wire tab switching into/out of Áudio to start/stop the recorder.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- `record: ^6.0.0` (new dependency) handles mic capture and permission (`hasPermission()`) — no separate `permission_handler`. Two new `capture/domain` ports, `MicRecorder` and `AudioTranscriber`, decouple the cubit from both packages (Code Map has the exact files).
+- `AudioTranscriber.transcribe()` returns `String?` — `null` means failure, a local-only outcome never wrapped in `Failure` (RNF09 scopes `Failure` to repository/backend calls).
+- `AudioEntryCubit` (new, own sealed `AudioCaptureState`, separate from `TextEntryState`) drives: idle → recording → processing → transcribed/error. Recording starts/stops from `InsertionModal`'s existing tab-switch listener. The recorded file is never deleted on a transcription or permission failure; "Tentar novamente" retries in place (re-transcribe the same file, or re-request permission if none was ever recorded).
+- `Entry`/`EntriesRepository.create`/its DTO/datasource/impl all gain an optional `int? mediaDurationSeconds` (sent/decoded only when non-null) — already reserved in `openapi.yaml`'s entries-create contract. `AudioEntryCubit.save()` calls `create(source: EntrySource.audio, ...)`, mirroring `TextEntryCubit.save()`'s `isClosed`/no-double-submit guards.
+- Every transition gets a screen-reader announcement, same `_announce` helper. `InsertionModal` provides both cubits (`MultiBlocProvider`) and closes both in `show()`'s `finally`.
+
+**Ask First:** none identified.
+
+**Never:**
+- Implement the full cross-tab cancel-safety rule (Story 3.4) — this story's trivial case: `create` only fires on explicit Salvar, and leaving the Áudio tab mid-recording stops the recorder (resource safety only, not 3.4's full choreography).
+- Send audio bytes to the backend in any call — transcription is 100% on-device (FR-12); only the resulting text reaches `entries-create`.
+- Build Story 3.3's Foto tab or touch its placeholder.
+- Add `permission_handler` or any separate permission package.
+- Write an automated test exercising the real `record`/`whisper_ggml` native plugins (no device/simulator exists, AGENTS.md) — both are mocked (mocktail) in `AudioEntryCubit` tests, same convention as `EntriesRepository` in `TextEntryCubit` tests.
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Happy path | Switch to Áudio, record, stop, review text, tap Salvar | Waveform animates while recording; freezes at 35% opacity while transcribing; text editable once transcribed; `POST /entries` (`source: audio`, `mediaDurationSeconds`) fires; success closes modal | N/A |
+| Transcription fails | `AudioTranscriber.transcribe` returns `null` | `AudioError` shown, audio file preserved, "Tentar novamente" re-transcribes the same file | No auto-retry |
+| Mic permission denied | `MicRecorder.start()` permission check fails | `AudioError` with permission-specific message; "Tentar novamente" re-requests permission | No file to preserve |
+| Save fails (incl. offline) | Salvar tapped from `AudioTranscribed`, `create` returns a `Failure` | Inline message from `Failure.message`; Salvar re-enabled, text/audio preserved | `Failure.fromCode`, no auto-retry |
+| Leave tab mid-recording | Switch to Texto/Foto while `AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing` | Recorder stopped/released; no `POST /entries` fires | N/A |
+

+## Code Map
+
+- `pubspec.yaml:52` -- add `record: ^6.0.0` beneath `whisper_ggml`.
+- `lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart` (new) -- abstract `MicRecorder` (start/stop→`(path, duration)`/cancel/amplitude stream) -- mirrors `EntriesRepository`'s port convention.

+/// (`AccountSettingsCubit`/`AuthCubit`, lazy singletons), [TextEntryCubit]/

diff --git a/lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart b/lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..dd7a605
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+// The constructor keeps a public named param (`recorder`) distinct from
+// the private field it initializes, matching
+// `vault_repository_impl.dart`'s documented convention.
+// ignore_for_file: prefer_initializing_formals
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:path_provider/path_provider.dart';
+// Aliased — `record`'s own `AudioRecorder` would otherwise clash with
+// nothing in this file today, but the alias keeps every reference to the
+// package explicit, per Code Map.
+import 'package:record/record.dart' as record_pkg;
+
+import '../../domain/services/mic_recorder.dart';
+
+/// Wraps `package:record`'s `AudioRecorder` behind the [MicRecorder] port.
+/// A `get_it` singleton (Code Map/`capture_injection.dart`) — one real
+/// recorder for the app's lifetime, reused across every Insertion Modal
+/// open, never recreated per "+" tap the way `AudioEntryCubit` itself is.
+class RecordMicRecorder implements MicRecorder {
+  RecordMicRecorder({required record_pkg.AudioRecorder recorder})
+    : _recorder = recorder;
+
+  final record_pkg.AudioRecorder _recorder;
+
+  /// Set by [start], cleared by [stop]/[cancel] — [stop] has no other way
+  /// to learn how long the session ran, since `AudioRecorder.stop()` only
+  /// ever returns the output path.
+  DateTime? _startedAt;
+
+  /// Set by [start], cleared by [stop]/[cancel] — tracked independently
+  /// of `_recorder`'s own "delete on cancel" contract (Review finding:
+  /// that contract was asserted in this class's own doc comment but
+  /// never independently verified) so [cancel] can delete the file
+  /// itself rather than relying solely on the plugin's behavior.
+  String? _currentPath;
+
+  @override
+  Future<bool> hasPermission() => _recorder.hasPermission();
+
+  @override
+  Future<void> start() async {
+    final dir = await getTemporaryDirectory();
+    final path =
+        '${dir.path}/cerne_audio_entry_'
+        '${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.wav';
+    await _recorder.start(
+      // 16kHz mono matches `whisper_ggml`'s own expected input exactly
+      // (its internal ffmpeg conversion step — `WhisperAudioConvert` —
+      // falls back to passing the file through unconverted when ffmpeg
+      // is unavailable, which only works if it's already in this shape).
+      const record_pkg.RecordConfig(
+        encoder: record_pkg.AudioEncoder.wav,
+        sampleRate: 16000,
+        numChannels: 1,
+      ),
+      path: path,
+    );
+    _startedAt = DateTime.now();
+    _currentPath = path;
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Future<MicRecording?> stop() async {
+    final path = await _recorder.stop();
+    final startedAt = _startedAt;
+    _startedAt = null;
+    _currentPath = null;
+    if (path == null || startedAt == null) {
+      return null;
+    }
+    return MicRecording(
+      path: path,
+      durationSeconds: DateTime.now().difference(startedAt).inSeconds,
+    );
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Future<void> cancel() async {
+    _startedAt = null;
+    final path = _currentPath;
+    _currentPath = null;
+    await _recorder.cancel();
+    // Review finding: don't rely solely on the plugin's own "cancel
+    // deletes the file" contract — delete it ourselves too, best-effort,
+    // so this class's own doc comment stays true regardless of the
+    // underlying plugin's actual behavior.
+    if (path != null) {
+      try {
+        await File(path).delete();
+      } catch (_) {
+        // Best-effort — the plugin may have already deleted it itself,
+        // or it may never have existed (e.g. a very early cancel).
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Stream<double> get amplitudeStream => _recorder
+      .onAmplitudeChanged(const Duration(milliseconds: 200))
+      .map(_normalize);
+
+  /// `record`'s own `Amplitude.current` is dBFS, roughly -45 (near
+  /// silence, in practice — the package's own floor is -160 but normal
+  /// mic noise never gets that quiet) to 0 (loudest) — rescaled to a
+  /// 0.0–1.0 range the waveform widget can use directly, with no
+  /// `package:record` type ever crossing the [MicRecorder] boundary.
+  double _normalize(record_pkg.Amplitude amplitude) {
+    const floorDb = -45.0;
+    final clamped = amplitude.current.clamp(floorDb, 0.0);
+    return (clamped - floorDb) / -floorDb;
+  }
+}

+/// Capture's on-device speech-to-text port — the `whisper_ggml`-backed
+/// `WhisperAudioTranscriber` is the only implementation (Code Map),
+/// mirroring [MicRecorder]'s same port convention.
+abstract class AudioTranscriber {
+  /// Transcribes the audio file at [audioPath] entirely on-device
+  /// (FR-12) — never sends audio bytes anywhere. `null` means failure (a
+  /// local-only outcome, never wrapped in `Failure` — RNF09 scopes
+  /// `Failure` to repository/backend calls); a non-null result is the
+  /// transcribed text, which may itself be empty if nothing was said.
+  Future<String?> transcribe(String audioPath);
+}

+/// A finished microphone recording — the on-disk file [path] plus its
+/// [durationSeconds], known only once [MicRecorder.stop] returns. Plain
+/// Dart, not `package:record`'s own types — keeps this port, and every
+/// caller that depends on it (`AudioEntryCubit`), decoupled from that
+/// package's shape (Boundaries: "decouple the cubit from both packages").
+class MicRecording {
+  const MicRecording({required this.path, required this.durationSeconds});
+
+  final String path;
+  final int durationSeconds;
+}
+
+/// Capture's own mic-recording port — the `record`-backed
+/// `RecordMicRecorder` is the only implementation (Code Map), mirroring
+/// `EntriesRepository`'s port convention (an abstract class in `domain/`,
+/// a concrete `data/` class wrapping the real package, injected via
+/// `capture_injection.dart`). `AudioEntryCubit` depends on this interface
+/// only, never on `package:record` directly (RNF06-style boundary,
+/// extended here to any native package, not just `data/`).
+abstract class MicRecorder {
+  /// Checks (and, per `record`'s own `AudioRecorder.hasPermission()`
+  /// default, requests if not yet granted) microphone permission — the
+  /// one permission check this story ever performs (Boundaries: "no
+  /// separate `permission_handler`"). `false` means denied/unavailable.
+  Future<bool> hasPermission();
+
+  /// Starts a new recording session to a fresh temp file. Callers must
+  /// have already confirmed [hasPermission] returns `true` — this method
+  /// itself doesn't re-check.
+  Future<void> start();
+
+  /// Stops the current recording session, returning its file path and
+  /// duration (whole seconds). `null` if no session was in progress.
+  Future<MicRecording?> stop();
+
+  /// Stops and discards (deletes) the current recording session, if any —
+  /// used only when leaving the Áudio tab mid-recording (I/O matrix:
+  /// "Recorder stopped/released", resource safety only, never the full
+  /// Story 3.4 cross-tab cancel choreography).
+  Future<void> cancel();
+
+  /// A normalized (0.0–1.0) amplitude sample roughly every 200ms while a
+  /// recording session is active — drives the waveform animation. No
+  /// guaranteed emissions outside an active session.
+  Stream<double> get amplitudeStream;
+}

+import '../../../entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart';
+import '../../domain/services/audio_transcriber.dart';
+import '../../domain/services/mic_recorder.dart';
+
+/// `AudioEntryCubit`'s own sealed state hierarchy — separate from
+/// `TextEntryState` (Boundaries: "own sealed `AudioCaptureState`,
+/// separate from `TextEntryState`"). Unlike `TextEntryState`, no common
+/// base-class field: the 5 variants don't share a uniform shape the way
+/// every `TextEntryState` always carries `activeTab`/`text` — [AudioIdle]
+/// genuinely has nothing in common with [AudioTranscribed], for instance.
+sealed class AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioCaptureState();
+}
+
+/// The state immediately after the modal opens on the Áudio tab exits
+/// (Never: this story's trivial cross-tab case), and the state a fresh
+/// `AudioEntryCubit` always starts in.
+class AudioIdle extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioIdle();
+}

+/// Recording in progress — [elapsedSeconds] backs the running monospace
+/// timer (Acceptance Criteria) and ticks once per second via
+/// `AudioEntryCubit`'s own internal `Timer.periodic`.
+class AudioRecording extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioRecording({required this.elapsedSeconds});
+
+  final int elapsedSeconds;
+}
+

+/// `InsertionModal`'s own `_AudioTab` freezes the waveform at 35% opacity
+/// for the whole duration of this state (Acceptance Criteria).
+class AudioProcessing extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioProcessing({required this.path, required this.durationSeconds});
+
+  final String path;
+  final int durationSeconds;
+}
+
+/// Transcription succeeded (even to an empty string) — [text] is editable
+/// before Salvar (Acceptance Criteria), mirrored into this state by
+/// `AudioEntryCubit.updateText` the same way `TextEntryCubit.updateText`
+/// mirrors the Texto field. [saving] is this story's `TextEntrySaving`
+/// equivalent folded into one state instead of a separate sibling class —
+/// both [path]/[durationSeconds] (needed for the eventual `create()` call)
+/// stay fixed across a save attempt, so there's nothing a sibling state
+/// would add that a boolean field doesn't already cover just as clearly.
+class AudioTranscribed extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioTranscribed({
+    required this.path,
+    required this.durationSeconds,
+    required this.text,
+    required this.saving,
+  });
+
+  final String path;
+  final int durationSeconds;
+  final String text;
+  final bool saving;
+
+  AudioTranscribed copyWith({String? text, bool? saving}) => AudioTranscribed(
+    path: path,
+    durationSeconds: durationSeconds,
+    text: text ?? this.text,
+    saving: saving ?? this.saving,
+  );
+}
+
+/// A save attempt from [AudioTranscribed] succeeded — `InsertionModal`'s
+/// listener reacts to this exactly like `TextEntrySaved` (announce, then
+/// pop). Terminal, same rationale as `TextEntrySaved`'s own doc.
+class AudioSaved extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioSaved();
+}
+
+/// The last attempt failed — covers all 3 failure rows of the I/O matrix:
+/// - Mic permission denied -> [path]/[durationSeconds] both `null` ("No
+///   file to preserve"); [AudioEntryCubit.retry] re-requests permission.
+/// - Transcription failed -> [path]/[durationSeconds] carry the preserved
+///   file; [AudioEntryCubit.retry] re-transcribes it, never re-records.
+/// - Save failed (incl. offline) -> same preserved [path]/
+///   [durationSeconds]/[text] semantics as `TextEntryError`; the modal's
+///   `_AudioTab` keeps showing the editable text with Salvar re-enabled
+///   rather than routing back through [AudioEntryCubit.retry].
+class AudioError extends AudioCaptureState {
+  const AudioError({
+    required this.path,
+    required this.durationSeconds,
+    required this.message,
+    this.text,
+  });
+
+  final String? path;
+  final int? durationSeconds;
+  final String message;
+
+  /// Non-null only for a save failure — lets `_AudioTab` keep rendering
+  /// the editable text field under the inline error, same as
+  /// `TextEntryError`'s own `_TextoTab` rendering.
+  final String? text;
+}
+
+/// Drives the Áudio tab's recording -> processing -> transcribed/error
+/// pipeline (Intent). A fresh, `get_it`-factory-scoped instance per "+"
+/// tap, same convention as `TextEntryCubit` — [MicRecorder]/

+  AudioEntryCubit(this._micRecorder, this._audioTranscriber, this._repository)

+  final AudioTranscriber _audioTranscriber;
+  final EntriesRepository _repository;
+
+  Timer? _elapsedTimer;
+
+  /// Bumped by [cancel] so an in-flight [startRecording]/[stopRecording]

+  /// the same role `isClosed` already plays for `close()`, but for a tab

+  int _generation = 0;
+

  Verification-gap findings:
  
  ### Full-modal dismiss never exercises the mic-release path it added
  
  - **Changed surface:** `InsertionModal.show()`'s `finally` block now calls `await audioCubit.cancel(); await audioCubit.close();` after `await cubit.close();` — `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:93-94`. The added comment states this exists specifically so the "x" button / swipe-down / barrier-tap dismiss of the *whole modal* (as opposed to a tab switch, which already goes through the tab-switch listener's own `cancel()` call at `insertion_modal.dart:221`) actually releases the native recording session.
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** the same dismiss gestures while `AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing` is active.
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_audio_test.dart` asserts `fakeMicRecorder.cancelCalls == 1` exactly once, at line 318 ("Leave tab mid-recording" test), which exercises the tab-switch listener's `cancel()` call, not `show()`'s `finally` block. Neither that file nor `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_test.dart` ever taps `Icons.close` (or otherwise pops the sheet) while the Áudio tab is recording/processing — `insertion_modal_test.dart`'s own `Icons.close` test ("Cancel before save") stays on the Texto tab the whole time. `AudioEntryCubit.close()` itself only cancels the elapsed-seconds `Timer` (`audio_entry_cubit.dart`'s `close()` override) and never touches `_micRecorder`, so it provides no safety net.
  - **Missing verification:** no test opens the modal, switches to Áudio (starts recording), taps the "x" (or otherwise dismisses the whole sheet), and asserts the recorder was actually canceled/released.
  - **Demonstration:** removing the `await audioCubit.cancel();` line from `show()`'s `finally` (reverting to pre-review behavior, which the diff's own comment says was broken) would leave the native recording session running after the "x"/swipe/barrier dismiss while recording — yet every test in both widget-test files would stay green, since that exact call path is never driven by any test.
  - **Consequence:** a regression that re-leaks the open mic session on full-modal dismiss (not just tab-switch) would ship undetected.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a `testWidgets` mirroring the existing "Leave tab mid-recording" test but dismissing via `Icons.close` instead of switching to "Texto", asserting `fakeMicRecorder.cancelCalls == 1`.
  
  ### Audio "saving" announcement has no regression test, unlike its Texto-tab twin
  
  - **Changed surface:** the `switch` in `_onAudioStateChange` has a dedicated `case AudioTranscribed(saving: true): _announce('Salvando registro');` ahead of the general `case AudioTranscribed(): _announce('Transcrição concluída...')` — `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:262-266` (the discriminator feeding the de-dup guard is the separate `_audioAnnounceKindOf` function at `insertion_modal.dart:120`, which independently maps `AudioTranscribed(saving: true)` to its own `.saving` kind).
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** a screen-reader user saving an audio entry — AGENTS.md's own acceptance line for this story requires "an announced label accompanies [every state change] — never color/animation alone."
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** the Texto tab's equivalent (`TextEntrySaving(): _announce('Salvando registro')`) has a dedicated test, `insertion_modal_test.dart:307` ("Salvar tapped announces 'Salvando registro'"). The Áudio tab's `announcements` group in `insertion_modal_audio_test.dart` only asserts "Gravando áudio", "Transcrevendo áudio", the transcribed-review prompt, a transcription-failure message, and "Registro salvo" — no test asserts "Salvando registro" is announced while an audio save is in flight.
  - **Missing verification:** no assertion that tapping Salvar on the Áudio tab announces "Salvando registro" before the eventual "Registro salvo".
  - **Demonstration:** deleting the `case AudioTranscribed(saving: true):` branch (leaving only the general `case AudioTranscribed():`) would make the switch announce the stale "Transcrição concluída. Revise o texto antes de salvar." message during an audio save instead of "Salvando registro" — a real wrong-announcement regression — yet no test in `insertion_modal_audio_test.dart` would fail, since none asserts on that specific announcement.
  - **Consequence:** a screen-reader user would hear the wrong status while an audio entry is saving, and this would ship undetected.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a `testWidgets` analogous to `insertion_modal_test.dart:307`, intercepting announcements, tapping Salvar on a transcribed audio entry, and asserting `contains('Salvando registro')`.
  
  ### Temp-file cleanup after a successful/abandoned audio recording is never observed
  
  - **Changed surface:** `AudioEntryCubit._deleteRecordingFile()` (`lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:437-443`), fire-and-forget (`unawaited`) called from `cancel()`'s mid-processing-abandon branch (`audio_entry_cubit.dart:356`) and from `save()`'s success branch (`audio_entry_cubit.dart:426`) — both added by this diff's review pass specifically to stop leaking a `.wav` file per recording (per the spec's own "Suggested Review Order" notes).
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** every successful audio save, and every abandoned mid-processing recording.
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** searched `test/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit_test.dart` (symbol `_deleteRecordingFile` is private, so no direct mock point) and the whole repo for `_deleteRecordingFile`/`File(path)`/`existsSync` — the only test that creates a real file and asserts it is deleted is `test/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder_test.dart:154-160`, which covers `RecordMicRecorder.cancel()`'s own delete call, a different class and call site entirely. Every `AudioEntryCubit` test (unit-level and the widget-level `insertion_modal_audio_test.dart`) uses fake string paths like `/tmp/a.wav` that never correspond to a real file, so `_deleteRecordingFile`'s `await File(path).delete()` silently no-ops inside its own `catch`, and neither the call nor its outcome is observed anywhere.
  - **Missing verification:** no test (real-file-based, the way `record_mic_recorder_test.dart` does it for the plugin wrapper) asserts the temp recording file is actually gone after a successful `save()` or after `cancel()` abandons a mid-processing recording.
  - **Demonstration:** deleting both `unawaited(_deleteRecordingFile(...))` call sites (or breaking `_deleteRecordingFile` itself) would silently leak one `.wav` file per successful audio save and per abandoned mid-processing recording — yet the full test suite would stay green, since no test observes this side effect.
  - **Consequence:** unbounded temp-file accumulation on-device would ship undetected.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a cubit-level test using a real temp file (same `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync` pattern as `record_mic_recorder_test.dart`) as the `MicRecorder.stop()`/`AudioProcessing` path, asserting `File(path).existsSync()` is `false` after a successful `save()` and after `cancel()` during `AudioProcessing`.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  - `_AudioTranscribedView`/`_AudioErrorView` (non-retry branch) both compute `canSave` from `controller.text.trim()` directly rather than from the cubit's own state text — this works today only because `onChanged` keeps the controller and cubit state in lockstep (`updateText`), but it means Salvar's enabled/disabled state is derived from widget-local mutable state rather than the single source of truth the rest of the pipeline uses (`lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart`'s `_AudioTranscribedView`/`_AudioErrorView`). Not a verification gap (no test relies on divergence) — just a latent coupling worth noting.
  - The `deferred-work.md` entry added by this diff already discloses that `TextEntryCubit.save()`'s `state is TextEntrySaved` double-tap guard (`lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart:119`) has no dedicated regression test; I independently confirmed this by reading `test/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit_test.dart` and `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_test.dart` — neither calls `save()`/taps Salvar more than once per test, so this gap is real but already self-reported in the diff.
  
</agent-message>

   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

[lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:330]

- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test asserts "Salvando registro" is announced while an audio save is in flight (the Texto tab's equivalent has one) [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:263]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_deleteRecordingFile` cleanup after a successful save or an abandoned mid-processing recording is never verified against a real file — every cubit/widget test uses fake paths that silently no-op the delete [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:437]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `stopRecording()` reads `_generation` but never bumps it on entry (unlike `startRecording()`) — a rapid double-tap on the stop control before the UI rebuilds can let a second, stale `_micRecorder.stop()` call overwrite a valid `AudioProcessing`/transcription result with a bogus `AudioError` [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:208]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `MicRecorder` native calls (`hasPermission`/`start`/`stop`/`cancel`) are never wrapped in try/catch — a thrown `PlatformException` escapes uncaught; inside `InsertionModal.show()`'s `finally`, that would also skip the following `audioCubit.close()` [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:161]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_Waveform`'s `amplitudeStream.listen()` has no `onError` handler — an error from the native amplitude stream becomes an uncaught async exception [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:945]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `RecordMicRecorder.stop()` computes `durationSeconds` via `DateTime.now().difference(startedAt).inSeconds` with no floor — a backward clock adjustment mid-recording yields a negative value, which the backend's `mediaDurationSeconds: minimum 0` contract will reject, turning an otherwise-successful recording into a save failure [lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart:73]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `AudioIdle` is the one `AudioCaptureState` transition never announced to screen readers (`case AudioIdle(): break;`) — masked today only because its one reachable path (tab-switch away while recording) coincides with the separate tab-switch announcement [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:278]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test covers `cancel()` racing a `retry()`-triggered re-transcription — appears already safe via `_transcribe`'s own state-based guard, but unverified by any test [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:282]

**Defer:**
- [x] [Review][Defer] No maximum recording duration is enforced anywhere — the elapsed-timer `MM:SS` label has no cap past 99 minutes and nothing bounds an unboundedly long on-device transcription; not called for anywhere in the spec's I/O matrix, a product/UX decision rather than a technical one [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:694] — deferred, out of this story's scope

content.text:
**Code review complete.** 1 `decision-needed`, 9 `patch`, 2 `defer`, 7 dismissed as noise.

Findings written to the review findings section in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-3-2-audio-entry-capture-on-device-transcription.md`.

All four review layers converged on one real bug (found independently by Blind Hunter, Acceptance Auditor, and partially Verification Gap), plus Edge Case Hunter surfaced a race condition and several unguarded native-call paths. I double-checked each claim against the actual code (and the backend contract) before rating — two Blind Hunter findings (`entry_dto.g.dart` regeneration, untested null-case in the datasource) turned out to be false positives once verified, so I dismissed them.

**Decision needed — your call:**

`AudioEntryCubit.cancel()` only deletes the orphaned temp `.wav` file for `AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing` states. If the user dismisses the *whole modal* (✕, swipe-down, or barrier tap — not a tab switch) while sitting in `AudioTranscribed` (reviewed, unsaved) or a file-carrying `AudioError` (failed save), the file is never deleted — and since `close()` runs right after, nothing will ever clean it up. It's a permanent orphan on disk.

The spec's I/O matrix only explicitly requires cleanup for "leave tab mid-recording" (the `AudioProcessing` case, already handled) — this is a scope question, not a correctness-is-obvious bug:

1. **Patch now** — extend `cancel()` to also delete the file for `AudioTranscribed`/file-carrying `AudioError`, treating any full-modal dismiss as "discard."
2. **Defer to Story 3.4** — that story owns the full cross-tab cancel-safety choreography; this is a bounded disk-space leak (small audio files), not data loss or a crash, so it can wait.
3. **Defer as its own backlog item** — real but low-urgency; don't bundle into 3.4's scope either.

**HALT** — reply with 1, 2, or 3.
PROCESSO: 1.

88:### Review Findings
91:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `AudioEntryCubit.cancel()` never deletes the temp recording file for `AudioTranscribed`/a file-carrying `AudioError` — dismissing the whole modal (not a tab switch) while reviewing transcribed text or after a failed save permanently orphans that `.wav` file, since `close()` runs right after and nothing will ever clean it up. `cancel()` only has cleanup branches for `AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing`. Decision: patch now (extend `cancel()`'s cleanup to these two states). [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:330]
92:- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test exercises full-modal dismiss (e.g. "x" tap) while `AudioRecording`/`AudioProcessing`, so the existing `audioCubit.cancel()` call in `InsertionModal.show()`'s `finally` has no regression coverage [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:94]
93:- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test asserts "Salvando registro" is announced while an audio save is in flight (the Texto tab's equivalent has one) [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:263]
94:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_deleteRecordingFile` cleanup after a successful save or an abandoned mid-processing recording is never verified against a real file — every cubit/widget test uses fake paths that silently no-op the delete [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:437]
95:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `stopRecording()` reads `_generation` but never bumps it on entry (unlike `startRecording()`) — a rapid double-tap on the stop control before the UI rebuilds can let a second, stale `_micRecorder.stop()` call overwrite a valid `AudioProcessing`/transcription result with a bogus `AudioError` [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:208]
96:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `MicRecorder` native calls (`hasPermission`/`start`/`stop`/`cancel`) are never wrapped in try/catch — a thrown `PlatformException` escapes uncaught; inside `InsertionModal.show()`'s `finally`, that would also skip the following `audioCubit.close()` [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:161]
97:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_Waveform`'s `amplitudeStream.listen()` has no `onError` handler — an error from the native amplitude stream becomes an uncaught async exception [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:945]
98:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `RecordMicRecorder.stop()` computes `durationSeconds` via `DateTime.now().difference(startedAt).inSeconds` with no floor — a backward clock adjustment mid-recording yields a negative value, which the backend's `mediaDurationSeconds: minimum 0` contract will reject, turning an otherwise-successful recording into a save failure [lib/features/capture/data/services/record_mic_recorder.dart:73]
99:- [ ] [Review][Patch] `AudioIdle` is the one `AudioCaptureState` transition never announced to screen readers (`case AudioIdle(): break;`) — masked today only because its one reachable path (tab-switch away while recording) coincides with the separate tab-switch announcement [lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:278]
100:- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test covers `cancel()` racing a `retry()`-triggered re-transcription — appears already safe via `_transcribe`'s own state-based guard, but unverified by any test [lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:282]
